title: lightweight-prefetch-fragmentation-scheduler-and-kv-stitcher-for-prefill-decode-handoff
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Prefill and decode stages interact poorly when we assume monolithic prefill windows. Long prefill windows improve throughput but hurt tail latency for short requests; small windows reduce batching efficiency for long contexts. This PR introduces a lightweight prefetch fragmentation scheduler (aka mini-window prefetcher) and a KV-stitcher handoff to decouple window sizing from decode scheduling and enable safe speculative priming.

Summary of changes: 1) mini-window prefetcher: runtime component that slices incoming prefill requests into micro-windows (configurable 'mini_size' default 32 tokens) based on per-model sequence-length histograms and recent workload signals. The scheduler emits fragment offers rather than forcing one atomic prefill window. 2) KV-stitcher: merge-layer that coalesces KV priming across adjacent or overlapping fragments to avoid redundant KV writes; performs cheap idempotent lookups before doing heavy priming. 3) Handshake protocol: offer/ack/activate with timeout and soft-fallback. The offering prefill can be accepted by decode if decode has capacity or stored as a warm fragment otherwise. This enables stage overlap without double-priming. 4) Speculative priming policy: conservative heuristics (weight by token-prob mass and recent tail-length distribution) allow spec prefill for low-cost fragments when latency SLO permits. 5) Kernel ordering hint: small change to the attention kernel launcher so primed KV pages are touched in an access-friendly order to improve memory locality during decode. 6) Backpressure/hysteresis: the scheduler tracks microfragment ack rate and inserts adaptive delays to avoid thrash when model load is spiky. 7) Telemetry and feature gates: telemetry events for fragment.offer/ack/activate/stitch, histograms of stitch success, and a runtime flag (runtime.prefetch.fragment.enabled) with staged rollout.

Design details and safety: - Prefetch fragments are self-describing (start_token, length, seed_hash) so KV-stitcher can detect overlapping ranges. Stitcher performs a fast bloom-check followed by a KV probe; on stitch hit it avoids priming and emits a 'stitch_hit' event. - Offer/ack includes a capacity token; decode may NACK with backpressure_hint indicating when to retry. NACKs are rate-limited to prevent retry storms. - Timeouts: fragments not activated within 150ms (configurable) are retained for a short ttl (default 500ms) for opportunistic reuse or evicted. - The speculative policy is opt-in per model and gated by a quality-signal that prevents spec prefills for models with high variance in output quality.

Performance: Microbenchmarks (internal perf-lab, rtx-a100 pool) show: - Short-context p95 latency reduced by ~12-18% for requests < 64 tokens due to reduced prefill tail. - Mixed workload throughput (80/20 long/short) improved effective tokens/sec by ~9% for batchable workloads because KV-stitcher reduced duplicate priming by 22%. - Worst-case decode latency impact on long contexts is negligible (+1-2% median) because stitcher coalesces fragments and kernel hint improves locality. Full perf runs and raw numbers attached in commits.

Test plan: unit tests for stitcher bloom/probe logic, property tests for fragment idempotency, integration tests exercising offer/ack/activate across the runtime (including NACK/backpressure), and an end-to-end perf canary in perf-canary that runs mixed workloads for 24h. Added tracing hooks to the console to visualize fragment lifecycle.

Rollout plan: feature gate off by default. Roll out to 5% of traffic for first 48h with increased sampling, then 25% if metrics stable, then 100%. Include automatic rollback if stitch_hit_rate < 10% or p95 regresses by >10%.

Related: ENG-4821 (prefetch fragmentation spike mitigation), ENG-5112 (kv cache duplication reduction). See linked perf-canary runs in perf-lab.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of mini-window scheduler and KV-stitcher
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Perf benchmarks and canary config
- [x] Telemetry and feature gating
- [x] Docs: short entry in serving/runtime/CHANGELOG and internal runway notes

Notes: This approach intentionally separates "how much we prefill" from "when decode consumes it" which gives the scheduler flexibility to optimize both latency and throughput independently. We kept the priming path idempotent and low-overhead to avoid introducing correctness risk.

fix(kv): implement Bloom pre-check and probe path for KV-stitcher
perf(kernel): add kernel touch-order hint for primed KV pages
test(prefetch): property tests for fragment idempotency
ci: enable canary pipeline config and telemetry events
review_comments: Miguel Ortega (2025-02-15): Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) add more explanation of trade-offs in docs (short/long context), (2) make the default mini_size configurable per-model. Response: updated config to be model-scoped and added section in CHANGELOG. - Asha

Jin Park (2025-02-17): Suggest tightening the default timeout from 200ms to 150ms based on lab runs. Also requested an explicit counter for NACKs to detect thrash. Response: lowered timeout and added nack_counter metric. - Asha
Leah Cohen (2025-02-18): Approve after tests and canary are green. Left small comment about bloom false-positive tuning. Response: tuned bloom parameters and added automated calibration job. - Asha
release_notes: Introduce a mini-window prefetcher and KV-stitcher to decouple prefill sizing from decode scheduling. Improves short-tail latency and reduces duplicate KV priming; gated behind runtime.prefetch.fragment.enabled. Rollout behind canary with automatic rollback criteria.
notes: This PR changes runtime behavior but is behind a feature flag; no breaking changes expected. Metric keys added: runtime.prefetch.fragment.stitch_hit_rate, runtime.prefetch.fragment.nack_count, runtime.prefetch.fragment.latency_ms.
